$comment: Rule catalog — record keeping. Standard 18. Every other rule in this pack is scoped to the recorded universe, which makes record.decision-record-required the assumption the rest of the catalog rests on.

rules.title: Every decision produces a record
rules.description: Every wagering decision — BET and PASS alike — produces a well-formed decision record carrying every pipeline stage value as it stood at decision time, with a unique identifier.
rules.rationale: This is the rule the rest of the catalog depends on. Every claim this pack makes is scoped to what was recorded, so an unrecorded wager is not merely undocumented: it is invisible to every exposure cap, every process metric, and every check in the system.
rules.remediation: Write a decision record for the wager. If the decision was a PASS, record it as one.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that recorded decisions are well-formed. It CANNOT establish that every decision was recorded — nothing inside a ledger can show what was left out of it. This is the pack's largest single limitation and it is load-bearing for exposure.no-cap-breaches, edge.threshold-respected, and every aggregate metric.

rules.title: A PASS is recorded with the same rigour as a BET
rules.description: A PASS produces a full decision record stating the gates that failed, or that it was discretionary, and stakes nothing.
rules.rationale: A ledger of BETs only cannot show that anything was ever declined, so it cannot distinguish a disciplined process from one that took every wager it looked at. Recorded PASSes are the evidence that the thresholds do something.
rules.remediation: Record the PASS with its reasons and a zero stake.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance over recorded PASSes. It cannot establish that every PASS was recorded, and an unrecorded PASS is the easiest omission of all — nothing happened, so nothing prompts the record.

rules.title: Results are appended, never merged into the decision
rules.description: Settlement information is recorded outside the decision block and carries a timestamp strictly after the decision's. No result field alters a decision-time value.
rules.rationale: This separation is what makes it possible to judge a decision by what was known when it was made. If a result could reach back into the decision block, every record would silently become a record of what should have been done.
rules.remediation: Move settlement information into the outcome block and leave the decision untouched.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance from the record structure and timestamp ordering.

rules.title: Historical recommendations are never silently altered
rules.description: No decision-time field is edited after the record is written. A correction is a new record referencing the original, never an amendment to it.
rules.rationale: Editing history after a result is known is how a betting record becomes a story about how well someone was doing. It is also the violation that destroys every other guarantee at once: once records can change, no metric computed from them means anything.
rules.remediation: Restore the original values and record the correction as a new record referencing the original.
rules.$assuranceNote: The decision digest detects any edit to a decision-time field after the record was written, and the policy digest detects a decision re-judged under thresholds it was not made under. Both are defeated by an edit made BEFORE the record was first written, and by rewriting the digest along with the content — the latter being visible in version control history rather than here.
